text: This in Bobwin fought his own government to start a mobile network. Today, he's the UK's first black billionaire, Meet Strive Masiywa. He came home from Britain in 1984 with an engineering degree. Took a job at the state phone company. Then quit and started his own engineering business with $75 he'd saved from his salary. The business did well, but he was watching something bigger. By his count, 7 and 10 Africans had never heard of phone ring and the state phone company told him mobile had no future. So he decided to build a network himself and called it Eaconette. Then a middleman for three government ministers told him a license would cost $400,000. He refused to pay and took the government to court instead. Then, President Robert Magaba used emergency powers meant for natural disasters to ban private mobile networks with two years in prison for anyone who built one. When the license finally went to tender, it went to a group linked to the president's nephew. Then his team found paperwork showing an official had cut 20% from Eaconette's score. In 1998, after five years in court, Eaconette switched on. The state phone company told him mobile had no future. He built the network anyway.
